summary: Importance of a job used to decide which tasks are served first when demand is over-subscribed. Affects assignment likelihood, not stop sequence.
range: Integer in the inclusive range [0, 100]. Default 0. Higher = more likely to be assigned when not all demand fits.
constraints: Integer within [0, 100]; values outside this range are invalid.
Higher value means the job is preferred for assignment under contention.
businessRules: Priority is a tiebreaker only: a higher-priority job with an impossible time window or a missing skill still goes to result.unassigned. Priority never overrides a hard constraint.
When jobs[].outsourcing_cost is present, the solver weighs it against priority in the assignment decision.

priority defines: Specify the priority of this job. The valid values are in the range of \[0, 100\]. Default value is 0. Please note that setting a priority will only decide whether this job will be assigned or not,…
Must stay consistent with: jobs.delivery, vehicles.capacity. Changes here may require validation of those fields.
Rule: Higher priority jobs are serviced first; ties break by job ID order.
Numeric field; verify sign (positive/negative) and unit from spec.
Optional field. Omitting uses solver's default behavior (no penalty).
validationRules: priority < 0 or priority > 100 -> input validation failed (HTTP 400).
testingGuidance: Boundary: priority 0 and 100 are valid extremes; 101 and -1 are invalid (expect HTTP 400).
Behavioral: an over-subscribed fleet where a high-priority and a low-priority job compete for the last slot -> the high-priority job is assigned, the low-priority one lands in result.unassigned.
Interaction: a high-priority job with an infeasible window is still unassigned (priority cannot rescue an infeasible task).
Interaction: Combination: tight capacity + one high-priority + one low-priority job competing for the last slot -> high-priority assigned, low-priority unassigned.
Interaction: Combination: high-priority job whose only skill is unavailable on any vehicle -> still unassigned despite priority.
Interaction: Interaction: two jobs with equal priority; one has outsourcing_cost 100, other 50 -> cost-based job assigned first.
